about.title: Personal Injury Help in Orinda, California
about.longDescription: Orinda's rolling roads and tree-lined lanes feed straight into SR-24, one of the busiest corridors linking this Contra Costa County community to the rest of the Bay Area. Public records show 78 injury collisions in the most recent final year, leaving 112 people hurt and, tragically, 1 person dead. Traffic tends to bunch up on Wednesday mornings between 7 and 9, when commuters merge onto SR-24 Eastbound and Westbound in a hurry to beat the backup. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the aftermath can be confusing — medical bills, missed work, insurance calls that seem to go nowhere. LawProactive is a free service that helps injured people in Orinda get connected with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, and we don't decide your case or promise any result. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Reaching out costs nothing and starts with a simple conversation about what you're dealing with.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Generally Have Two Years
items.desc: California law gives most injury victims two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. If a government entity is involved — say, a road defect — that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for a crash, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary injury cases, so your recovery isn't artificially capped.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency — they only get paid if you recover money, so there's no bill to worry about while you focus on healing.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Orinda?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. That window can shrink to as little as six months if a government agency is involved, such as a claim over road conditions, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: I was partly at fault for the accident — can I still recover money?
items.answer: Yes. California uses pure comparative fault, which means your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you aren't barred from recovering just because you share some blame.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Orinda?
items.answer: Public collision records show that reported crashes tend to peak on Wednesdays between 7 and 9 a.m., with higher volumes on corridors like SR-24, SR-24 Eastbound, and SR-24 Westbound. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service — we don't charge you to connect with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if they win money for you.

items.question: What if my injuries didn't seem serious right away?
items.answer: Some injuries, like whiplash or concussions, can take days to fully show symptoms. It's still worth talking to an attorney promptly, both for your health and because California's filing deadlines don't wait for symptoms to appear.
